Installation and troubleshooting

This guide is based on the original installation notes supplied with the project. It corrects commands that would otherwise fail and provides solutions for common Conda, R, Jupyter, and PASTRI installation errors.

Using a dedicated Conda environment is recommended because it keeps the PASTRI runtime separate from system-level R and Python installations.

1. Create the Conda environment

Run the following commands in Anaconda Prompt, Miniconda Prompt, or another terminal in which Conda has been initialized:

conda create -n PASTRI r-base=4.2.3 python=3.10 -c conda-forge
conda activate PASTRI

The original notes used conda create -n R4.2.3_test without specifying the packages to install, and onda activate was missing the initial c. Python 3.6 is no longer recommended because it has reached end of life and is often incompatible with current Jupyter dependencies.

Verify the environment:

conda info --envs
R --version
python --version

The active environment should have an asterisk (*) beside its name. R should report version 4.2.3 and Python should report version 3.10.x.

2. Install the Jupyter kernels

Install and register the Python kernel:

python -m pip install --upgrade pip ipykernel
python -m ipykernel install --user --name PASTRI --display-name "Python (PASTRI)"

Start R:

R

Install and register the R kernel from the R console:

install.packages("IRkernel", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
IRkernel::installspec(
  name = "pastri",
  displayname = "R 4.2.3 (PASTRI)",
  user = TRUE
)

Exit R and verify that Jupyter can find both kernels:

jupyter kernelspec list

3. Install PASTRI

Run the following commands in the R console:

install.packages("remotes", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
remotes::install_github(
  "yuxiaochen11/PASTRI",
  dependencies = TRUE,
  upgrade = "never"
)

library(PASTRI)
packageVersion("PASTRI")

To install PASTRI from a local source checkout instead:

install.packages("devtools", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
devtools::install(".")

Run the final command from the PASTRI project root, which is the directory containing the DESCRIPTION file.

4. Common errors

conda: command not found or Conda is not recognized as a command

Cause: Conda is not installed, or the current shell has not been initialized for Conda.

Solution:

  1. Use Anaconda Prompt or Miniconda Prompt.
  2. Alternatively, run conda init from a terminal that can already locate Conda.
  3. Close and reopen the terminal, then run conda activate PASTRI.

EnvironmentNameNotFound: Could not find conda environment

Cause: The environment has not been created, or its name was entered incorrectly.

Solution:

conda info --envs
conda create -n PASTRI r-base=4.2.3 python=3.10 -c conda-forge
conda activate PASTRI

Use the same environment name, PASTRI, in all subsequent commands.

PackagesNotFoundError: r-base=4.2.3

Cause: The requested R version is not available from the currently configured default channels.

Solution:

conda create -n PASTRI r-base=4.2.3 python=3.10 -c conda-forge

You can also configure conda-forge before creating the environment:

conda config --add channels conda-forge
conda config --set channel_priority strict

No module named pip or No module named ipykernel

Cause: The command is using Python from another environment, or the required package is not installed in the active environment.

Solution:

conda activate PASTRI
conda install pip ipykernel -c conda-forge
python -m pip show ipykernel

Using python -m pip instead of pip helps ensure that packages are installed for the Python interpreter in the active environment.

there is no package called 'IRkernel'

Cause: IRkernel is not installed in the active R library, or Jupyter and R are being run from different environments.

Solution:

install.packages("IRkernel", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
IRkernel::installspec(
  name = "pastri",
  displayname = "R 4.2.3 (PASTRI)",
  user = TRUE
)

Run .libPaths() in R to check which package libraries are active.

installation of package ... had non-zero exit status

Cause: An R dependency, compiler, or system library is usually missing. Search upward in the installation log for the first ERROR; the final line is often only a summary.

Recommended checks:

  1. Reactivate the PASTRI environment.
  2. Install the missing R package named near the first error.
  3. On Windows, install Rtools42 for R 4.2.x.
  4. On Linux, install the development library identified by the first error.
  5. Run remotes::install_github(..., dependencies = TRUE) again.

On Windows, check whether R can find the build tools:

install.packages("pkgbuild", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = TRUE)

package 'PASTRI' is not available for this version of R

Cause: install.packages("PASTRI") searches CRAN, but PASTRI is currently installed from GitHub or a local source checkout.

Solution:

install.packages("remotes", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
remotes::install_github("yuxiaochen11/PASTRI", dependencies = TRUE)

Error: Failed to install 'unknown package' from GitHub

Cause: GitHub may be unreachable, the repository address may be incorrect, the GitHub API rate limit may have been reached, or authentication may be missing.

Diagnostic installation command:

remotes::install_github(
  "yuxiaochen11/PASTRI",
  dependencies = TRUE,
  upgrade = "never",
  build_vignettes = FALSE
)

If the log reports an API rate limit, create a GitHub Personal Access Token and configure it in R:

install.packages("gitcreds", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()

Never store a token in a script, README, or Git commit.

'mc.cores' > 1 is not supported on Windows

Cause: Windows does not support the fork-based multicore implementation used by parallel::mclapply().

Solution: Explicitly request one core. PASTRI’s high-level functions also fall back to one core automatically on Windows.

node_pair_depth <- calculate_lca_depths(tree.path, mc.cores = 1)

result <- get_optimal_transition_matrix(
  node_pair_depth = node_pair_depth,
  cell_info = cell_info,
  Sel_u = "lca_normalized_height",
  fi_depth = 0.2,
  Bound_Matrix = bound_matrix,
  cell_type_list = cell_types,
  mc.cores = 1
)

object 'node_info' not found or object 'bound_matrix' not found

Cause: A partial example from a function reference page was executed without first creating its input objects.

Solution: Run the complete Quick start example in the README. Confirm that the required objects exist:

ls()
str(node_pair_depth)
str(cell_info)
str(bound_matrix)

subscript out of bounds, incompatible matrix dimensions, or an all-zero result

Common causes:

  • cell_type_list and Bound_Matrix use different dimensions or ordering.
  • Tree tip labels do not match cell_info$nodeLabel.
  • A selected cell type has no record with cellNum == 1.
  • No depth value satisfies u <= fi_depth.
  • The constraint matrix accidentally forbids every candidate direction.

Checks:

stopifnot(
  nrow(bound_matrix) == length(cell_types),
  ncol(bound_matrix) == length(cell_types)
)

setdiff(cell_types, unique(cell_info$celltype[cell_info$cellNum == 1]))
setdiff(node_pair_depth$node1, cell_info$nodeLabel)
range(node_pair_depth$lca_normalized_height, na.rm = TRUE)

The output matrix uses destinations as rows and sources as columns. To forbid a transition from C5 to C4, set:

bound_matrix["C4", "C5"] <- 0

Jupyter does not show R 4.2.3 (PASTRI)

Cause: The kernel was not registered, was registered for another user, or Jupyter is being run from another environment.

Solution:

conda activate PASTRI
jupyter kernelspec list

Then start R from the active environment and register the kernel again:

IRkernel::installspec(
  name = "pastri",
  displayname = "R 4.2.3 (PASTRI)",
  user = TRUE
)

5. Minimum diagnostic information

When opening an issue or requesting help, include the following output after removing usernames, tokens, and other sensitive information:

sessionInfo()
.libPaths()
packageVersion("PASTRI")

Also include the following terminal output:

conda info --envs
conda list
jupyter kernelspec list

Include the complete part of the installation log beginning at the first ERROR, together with the smallest code example that reproduces the problem.
